_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_as_of: 2026-08-14 · Sky157 — the sign-in door is back (it's in ℹ About now), and every locked tab finally offers a way in.
_status: You couldn't sign in to the new Admin tab, and the reason turned out to be worse than a broken button: the Team & RACI tab had kept the whole magic-link sign-in EXCEPT the button, so nothing could reach it — while Admin cheerfully told you to go use it there. The personal sign-in now lives in the ℹ About menu in the header, reachable from every tab, and Admin offers the same box right on its own page so it never sends you anywhere. Then we asked the bigger version of your question and counted: 43 tables need a phrase, 26 of them just to READ, and eight tabs offered neither a box nor even a hint of where the 🔒 button is — those tabs didn't look locked, they looked broken. There is now one shared unlock banner with a working box in it, and a test that fails the build if a new tab ever ships without one. Separately, SkyCode's noncredit CIP work found that a rule we'd shipped (every noncredit program gets 32.0111) was wrong for most programs; it was reverted within about twenty minutes, and the good news is the college data was right all along — what looked like 1,796 wrong codes were correct secondary codes.

items.text: Sign in once, in a real browser: click ℹ About in the header, type your email, press "Email me a link", then follow the link. You should land back on the tab you started from, already signed in — and Admin should open instead of turning you away. Nothing in this change has been tried outside a simulated browser, so this is the one thing worth five minutes.
Ask Jenni to confirm the Basic Skills code pairing. This single answer unblocks the first three build phases of the noncredit CIP work — nothing else on that list is holding as much up.

Also for Jenni: two codes are in real use but missing from her list — 32.0199 (60 programs) and 35.0101 (16). And the big one: can a non-CDCP category be CTE at all? That affects about 1,300 programs, and CTE is the funding line.

Decide where a confirmed noncredit category gets saved. Right now the plan was the browser's own storage, which is wrong for something that affects funding — it vanishes on another machine and nobody can see who decided what. Recommend a proper table that records who confirmed it and when.

Make the COBI header accessible and mobile-friendly, and drop the superscript from the logo. The superscript C is genuinely impossible — Unicode has no superscript capital C, so "CPL" renders as "cPL" and no font fixes it. Sam's call: plain, unbolded org name instead.

The link preview in Teams/Outlook comes from the page title, not the page itself — and those previews never run our code, so the org you picked can't change what they show. Making the preview follow the selected org needs a separate small page per org. Worth confirming Sam wants that before building it.

Sam wants to edit the Project Description in the ℹ About menu — it has gone stale as the project grew. It can't be edited in the page: the daily job rewrites that block every morning. The editor has to change where the daily job READS the description from.

Six new decision rights are on the register with nobody's name against them. Start with DR-13, the workplan itself — it is the most public thing the project publishes, four of its tables can be edited in the page by anyone holding the team phrase, and a wrong figure reaches the live dashboard on the next morning's run.

Still open from last session: drag a menu item, press Save, reload. The Admin tab has never been used in a real browser. Worst case is the menu you already have, and "Reset to how it ships" puts everything back.

Sierra named 1 of 9 D1.1 welding credentials and nobody has worked out why yet. Measure first: either the search never returned the other eight, or it found them and the answer only mentioned the best one. Those are different bugs with different fixes.
